title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Power
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: A cyberattack has kept a Chilean solar-and-battery plant off the grid for almost three months, and no one has said which control systems were hit
items.content_text: Chile’s National Electric Coordinator still lists the 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant in Tarapacá, and its 98 MW / 312 MWh battery system, at zero availability in its 14 November report, recorded as a forced outage caused by a cyberattack. The coordinator activated its disconnection protocol on 27 August after the company reported the incident; T13 dates the attack to 26 August. The same records show a cyber-caused forced disconnection of a transformer at the Santa Rita substation that day. On 11 November a member of Congress asked which systems (SCADA, protection, inverters, battery management) were compromised and whether notification duties were met; no answer had been published by 16 November. Owner, entry route and attacker are undisclosed. A plant disconnected for safety can stay dark for months if it cannot show its control systems are clean (editorial assessment).

_otthreatfeed.category: Top Story
_otthreatfeed.source_name: ESS News / pv magazine (17 Nov 2026, citing Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional records); T13 (16 Nov 2026, in Spanish); pv magazine Latin America (16 Nov 2026, congressional requests, in Spanish)
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Ongoing — still offline per 14 Nov 2026 coordinator report; congressional requests 11 Nov 2026; reported 16–17 Nov 2026; attack 26 Aug 2026

items.title: Norway says the Equinor and Skagerak Energi intrusions came through Microsoft’s Azure API Management cloud service
items.content_text: Norway’s National Security Authority (NSM) says an unidentified actor has been stealing secrets from Microsoft Azure API Management (APIM), and that Equinor and Skagerak Energi, a power and renewables utility in eastern Norway, were among several organisations hit. Equinor detected its intrusion on 17 November and contained it by 20 November; Skagerak disclosed its attack on 18 November. Both say oil, gas and electricity production carried on normally. SecurityWeek reports that Microsoft found the flaw in older “Classic” APIM tiers on 18 November and closed the access path a day later; exposed items include named-value secrets, identity-provider client secrets, subscription keys and management API tokens. No CVE has been issued. NSM advises treating those secrets as compromised. Utilities that move metering, dispatch or market data through cloud APIs should rotate them now (editorial assessment).

items.title: Peninsula Energy confirms attackers reached plant and wellfield control systems at its Wyoming uranium site, which is shut down
items.content_text: Peninsula Energy, an ASX-listed uranium producer, said on 25 November that the cyber incident found late on 20 November affected the plant and wellfield operating and control systems at its Lance in-situ recovery project in Crook County, Wyoming. The site has been shut down while the investigation continues, and the company’s shares are suspended until 30 November. Its US and Australian administrative systems were earlier reported as unaffected. Peninsula has not said how the attackers got in, what they did inside the control systems or when it expects to restart, and no group has claimed the attack. No effect on any power plant is reported. Lance produces uranium for nuclear fuel, so this is a confirmed OT shutdown in the generation fuel chain (editorial assessment).

items.title: Switzerland confirms its first AI-agent cyberattacks on critical infrastructure, with electricity providers among the targets
items.content_text: Switzerland’s Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) said on 26 November that five attacks in recent days used AI agents, frameworks that find weaknesses, pick tools and plan their next steps largely on their own. Four of the five compromised systems. Three targets were critical-infrastructure operators, which public broadcaster SRF identified as electricity, water and telecommunications providers. BACS named no victims or attacker and has not said whether any control systems were reached, or which of the targets were among the successful cases. The reported entry points were ordinary: default or easily guessed passwords and known flaws in internet-facing systems. The UK NCSC described the same pattern on 24 November. For generation and grid operators, exposed remote-access portals, HMIs and vendor accounts with weak passwords will now be found far faster (editorial assessment).

items.title: South Korea’s state power utility KEPCO confirms about 1.5 million records stolen, as turbine maker Suzlon reports its own incident
items.content_text: Korea Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) confirmed on 22 November that an attacker got into its internal network and reached two systems: its KEPCO ON customer billing and payment platform and its supplier procurement system. It detected the intrusion on 20 November, cut external access and suspended the affected services. The company says data on about 650,000 customers, 427,000 supplier representatives and 443,000 employees was exposed, roughly 1.52 million people. It has not said how the attacker got in, and a forum actor’s 19 November claim is unverified. No effect on power supply is reported. A day later India’s Suzlon Energy disclosed a cyber incident and said business-critical applications were unaffected. Procurement systems hold supplier contacts and project details that make good phishing material for grid vendors (editorial assessment).

items.title: Attackers rooted unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell, planted backdoors and wiped a VMware host; the root flaw is now in KEV
items.content_text: Check Point Research said on 12 November that attackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws on unpatched Check Point Mobile Access portals from 30 October, then used a local flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to become root. They planted backdoors, pivoted to a VMware ESXi host and ran a wiper. The first wave hit Israeli organizations, some destructively; a second wave from 2 November reached several countries without destruction. Attribution is unconfirmed (tooling resembles China-nexus UNC5221). CISA added the root flaw to KEV on 13 November. No OT victim is reported, but these firewalls often sit at the IT/OT boundary and ESXi often hosts HMIs and historians (editorial assessment).

items.title: Osaki Electric confirms data left its network and plans a staged restart of smart-meter production from 27 November
items.content_text: Osaki Electric, a Japanese smart-meter maker, found ransomware on 17 November and suspended production and shipments at its Saitama centre and two group plants. The company has said the intruder most likely got in on 15 November by password guessing against a VPN account without multi-factor authentication. In a 25 November filing it confirmed data was sent to an external destination, and set out a staged restart of production from 27 November, with shipments planned from 1 and 7 December. A Qilin leak-site claim has not been verified. Production equipment and meters already in the field are reported unaffected. For utilities the exposure is supplier-side: delayed meter rollouts and questions about the systems that build and sign device firmware (editorial assessment).

items.title: Illinois investigates an apparent cyberattack attempt on the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River
items.content_text: The Illinois Department of Natural Resources said on 20 November that it detected an apparent attempted cyberattack on the Algonquin Dam, about 45 miles northwest of Chicago, on 16 November. Staff blocked the unauthorised access at once, and the dam stayed secure and fully operational. IDNR has not said which system was targeted or whether gate controls were reachable. Illinois State Police, state agencies and CISA are investigating; no link to other attacks and no group has been named. For dam owners, hydro operators included, it is a prompt to check who can reach gate and spillway controls remotely (editorial assessment).

items.title: DHS tells Congress Iran-backed hackers have stepped up attacks on US water, energy and transport since February, while officials rule out hacking in last week’s outages
items.content_text: In written testimony for a House Homeland Security Committee hearing on 18 November, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Iranian state-sponsored groups and pro-Iranian criminals have targeted US critical infrastructure since the conflict with Iran began in February, with transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services increasingly in their sights. He described the attacks so far as mostly localized, low-damage disruptions of poorly secured industrial control systems. Officials said they found no evidence that hackers caused last week’s Microsoft 365 outage or the FAA ground stop. Separately, AttackIQ research (17 November) describes Iranian groups handing network access to one another, with espionage footholds later passed to teams pursuing destructive goals, often via contractors and suppliers. The official US view now matches France’s: Iran is going after the weakest exposed controllers (editorial assessment).

items.title: FBI warns criminals are using an AI-driven intrusion framework, ARTEX, against energy and other critical infrastructure, and a Texas regulator tells energy firms to harden now
items.content_text: On 18 November Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian urged producers, pipeline operators and energy firms to harden their defences, citing recent outages and a 13 November FBI IC3 advisory on ARTEX. The FBI describes ARTEX as an AI-driven autonomous penetration-testing framework that malicious actors have used to automate stages of an intrusion, with targets including energy, government, financial services and other critical infrastructure. Christian said ARTEX “may not be the only explanation” for the outages; no causal link has been established, and no Texas victim, incident or CVE has been named. The commission regulates oil and gas, not electricity, but the targeting applies equally to generators and transmission owners. Automated tooling shortens the time between an exposed service and an intrusion, so exposure reviews need to run continuously, not yearly (editorial assessment).

items.title: An AI-assisted crew broke into Check Point firewall management servers at more than 20 organisations, including energy companies
items.content_text: GreyNoise reported that a crew it tracks as GT13, using AI-assisted tooling, breached Check Point Security Management servers at no fewer than 22 organisations between 17 October and 2 November, with energy, transport and manufacturing among the sectors hit, according to Cybersecurity Dive on 24 November. Victims are not named and no OT impact is reported. A management server holds the policy for every gateway it controls, so whoever owns it can quietly change the rules at the IT/OT boundary. This is separate from the gateway-level PHP2Shell intrusions (see Incidents & Attacks), but it hits the same product family. Power-sector relevance is editorial assessment.

items.title: Dragos counts 1,266 ransomware attacks on industrial organizations in Q3, up 11%, and found no case of an operator touching a control system
items.content_text: Dragos said on 16 November that ransomware hit 1,266 industrial organizations between July and September 2026, up 11% on the second quarter, while the number of brands claiming industrial victims rose from 70 to 99. Manufacturing took 69% of cases; the ICS ecosystem of integrators, engineering firms and equipment makers logged 116. Qilin and The Gentlemen drove 29% of the total. Dragos saw no Q3 case of a ransomware operator manipulating a control system: production stopped because the IT, ERP and virtualization layers plants rely on went down. Entry came through edge devices and enterprise applications exploited within days of disclosure, and through stolen VPN and firewall credentials. For generators, being able to run the plant without those IT layers is the main defence (editorial assessment).

items.title: Siemens adds WTV676 and WTV776 metering gateways to its PHP2Shell advisory, while parts of Spectrum Power still have no fix
items.content_text: Siemens revised SSA-166980 on 16 and 18 November to add its WTV676 and WTV776 metering gateways to the products affected by PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both in CISA KEV); WTV676-HB6035 is fixed in firmware FW6.9.22-3.4, while WTV776-HB6035 has no fix. Grid-control parts also remain unfixed: Spectrum Power 4 with Nagios or Zabbix, Web Office Portal V3.0 to V3.2, HISViews V1.0, AMIS TS and two blueplanet 360 NX3 M6 models; Energy Engage V2.0SP9 will get no fix. Spectrum Power 3, 7 and TG and Energy Engage V3.1SP1 take PHP updates. ABB lists Netcontrol RTUs and ASPECT gateways, Schneider a Foxboro DCS server. No vendor product is reported exploited, but the same flaws have rooted PAN-OS and Check Point gateways (see Incidents & Attacks), so an exposed web front end next to grid control is a real foothold (editorial assessment).

items.title: Attackers try to plant bots on Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 edge gateways through a CVSS 10 Node-RED flaw
items.content_text: VulnCheck reported that from 30 October attackers tried to exploit CVE-2026-58115 against its honeypots. The CVSS 10.0 flaw is missing authentication in the Node-RED HTTP interface on SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed: an unauthenticated attacker can create flows that run code with maximum privileges. Early attempts deployed a flow that downloaded a Linux bot; later ones used a two-stage downloader, and some added an HTTP endpoint wired to an exec node, a backdoor that survives a reboot. Siemens published SSA-834709 in August; the fix is Node-RED 4.3.4.1 or later, or removing Node-RED. Only honeypots were hit, and no compromise of a real device has been reported. IoT2050 boxes serve as data-collection gateways at substations and generation sites, so look for ones you did not know about (editorial assessment).

items.title: A vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day for two months before Broadcom’s 19 November patch; vCenter 7.0 gets no fix
items.content_text: Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123890 on 19 November, a critical flaw in vCenter’s directory service that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker obtain an administrator session. Google’s Mandiant, which reported it, says a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited it for more than two months beforehand. In the cases Mandiant investigated, the group got in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw, attacked vCenter in early September with a custom tool called Bonesaw, stole SAML signing material and the vCenter master key, forged tokens and moved on to ESXi hosts. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; end-of-life vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. No victims or sectors are named. Plants that run HMIs, historians and engineering workstations as virtual machines should treat vCenter as part of OT (editorial assessment).

items.title: Java4Shell exploitation attempts begin, and Siemens tells customers to take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
items.content_text: Probing for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption bug in how OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later decode Base64 data, started within two days of its 17 November disclosure. GreyNoise counted more than 150 matching requests from five addresses by early 19 November and Previdian logged nine attempts from six addresses; none is confirmed to have succeeded. Exploitation needs a recent Intel or AMD x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI, and researchers at Calif showed unauthenticated code execution against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak setups, each with a tailored chain. For OT teams the key item is Siemens advisory SSA-272816: three Industrial Edge Management products are affected, fixes are in progress, and Siemens recommends taking those instances offline until they are patched. Cisco lists more than a dozen products with no fix yet, and Atlassian Data Center products are also unpatched.

items.title: A Brotli flaw already in CISA’s exploited list turns up in Siemens WinCC, WinCC OA and BRAUMAT, and most products have no fix yet
items.content_text: CISA republished Siemens’ assessment of CVE-2026-111497, a flaw in the widely used Brotli compression library, as an ICS advisory on 17 November. The out-of-bounds write in the decoder can crash the software, leak information or possibly allow code execution. CISA added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 27 October because of attacks elsewhere; nobody has reported exploitation through a Siemens product. Affected products include BRAUMAT and SISTAR V8.2, WinCC OA V3.20 and V3.21, WinCC Runtime Professional, WinCC V7/V8 and TIA Administrator. Fixes exist only for BRAUMAT/SISTAR (V8.2 Update 5) and WinCC OA V3.20 (P17.1). WinCC OA runs as SCADA in grid control rooms, substations and renewable plants, so power operators should prioritise it while most sites rely on the workaround (editorial assessment).

items.title: Hitachi Energy TRO600 wireless routers let an unauthenticated attacker read configuration and password files; firmware 9.2.2.1 fixes it
items.content_text: CISA republished Hitachi Energy advisory 8DBD000224 on 29 October as ICSA-26-302-02 (vendor date 27 October). It covers firmware for TRO600 series industrial wireless communications devices used by utilities, oil and gas companies and mining operators. CVE-2026-106087 (CVSS v3.1 7.5; v4.0 8.7) is missing authentication: an unauthenticated attacker can read or download arbitrary files, including configuration files and password data, in firmware 9.1.1.0 and earlier. CVE-2026-10756 (v3.1 7.5; v4.0 7.7) lets an authenticated attacker use port forwarding to get past network access restrictions, in 9.2.1.6 and earlier. Firmware 9.2.2.1 fixes both and is recommended. The advisory summary mentions remote code execution, but neither flaw description does. CISA lists the Energy sector and reports no known exploitation. Stolen router configurations could map the way into substations and remote sites (editorial assessment).

items.title: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 HMI programming software can be taken over by a booby-trapped project file
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-328-01 (24 November) covers the C-More EA9 programming software that engineers use to build screens for AutomationDirect’s EA9 touch-panel HMIs. CVE-2026-127280 (CVSS 7.8) is a heap-based buffer overflow: opening a crafted project file in version 6.80 or earlier can let an attacker run code on the engineering workstation. CISA lists critical manufacturing, energy and water among the sectors using the product and reports no known exploitation. The risk is the engineering laptop, which often holds credentials and project files for many sites. Small generators, substations and plant balance-of-plant panels are where EA9 HMIs tend to turn up (editorial assessment).

items.title: Schneider fixes a project-file flaw in Power Build Rapsody, the tool used to design low-voltage switchboards
items.content_text: CISA republished Schneider Electric’s advisory for EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody on 24 November (Schneider first published it on 10 November). Panel builders, engineering firms and utility design teams use the software to design and quote low-voltage switchboards. A use-after-free flaw in how it handles SSD project files (CVE-2026-119055) is triggered when a user opens a crafted file and can corrupt memory on that workstation. It is rated Medium (CVSS v4 4.6, v3.1 5.3) because it needs local access and user action. Schneider has issued fixed builds per language edition, for example 2.9.12.0101 (French) and 2.9.5.0000 (Spanish). No exploitation is reported. The practical exposure is project files swapped with contractors, so treat them like any untrusted attachment (editorial assessment).

items.title: The first standards behind the EU Cyber Resilience Act are out, setting the yardstick for relays, RTUs, inverters and other grid equipment sold in Europe
items.content_text: BSI announced on 23 November the publication of EN 40000-1-1, a shared vocabulary, and EN 40000-1-2, which sets principles, product risk assessment and lifecycle activities for products with digital elements. They are the first two of four horizontal standards supporting the EU Cyber Resilience Act; vulnerability handling (EN 40000-1-3) is due early 2027 and generic security requirements (EN 40000-1-4) later in 2027. Manufacturers’ reporting duties for exploited vulnerabilities have applied since September 2026, and from 11 December 2027 connected products placed on the EU market must meet the Act in full, including CE marking. Utilities buying protection relays, RTUs, inverters and substation gear can start asking suppliers how they are mapping products to these standards (editorial assessment).

items.title: Comments close 30 November on NIST’s draft rewrite of its OT security guide, a reference many utility auditors and insurers use
items.content_text: NIST’s draft Revision 4 of SP 800-82, the US government’s main guide to operational technology security, is open for public comment until 30 November 2026. The draft reorganises the guide around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with risk management now led by the Govern function, and adds sector material for building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels, and industrial IoT connected to cloud services. It also expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and detection, protecting system-management functions, and applying zero-trust principles. Many regulators, insurers and auditors use 800-82 as a reference, so its final wording can shape what operators are asked to show; the comment window is the chance for practitioners to flag guidance that would not work on a plant floor.
